text: Which limitation applies specifically to cell-free expression and would NOT apply to an equivalent cell-based (in vivo) experiment?
choices: Inability to model cell growth dynamics or predict promoter strength effects that depend on chromosome copy number
Inability to tolerate toxic reaction products
A mandatory multi-day cell transformation step before any measurement can be taken
Complete absence of transcription or translation machinery in the reaction
explanation: Because cell-free reactions contain no dividing cells, they cannot model growth dynamics, long-term genetic stability, or promoter behavior tied to chromosome copy number -- limitations explicitly listed for cell-free but not applicable to living cells. Toxic-product tolerance is actually an advantage of cell-free (not a shared limitation), the lengthy transformation step is a cell-based drawback that cell-free avoids, and cell-free reactions by definition do contain transcription/translation machinery, whether extracted or reconstituted.
